text:
Nashville's seven-game winning streak ended on the West Coast and then got buried in Minnesota on Tuesday, 7-3. That's a rough week, but it doesn't erase the run that came before it, capped by Roman Josi's shootout winner against Vegas and Juuse Saros's first shutout of the season.

Saros has been the reason. He's at .943 with 4.8 goals saved above expected over his last five starts, and the Predators have allowed about nine fewer goals than their chances against suggest this season. That's how a team with 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and 47% at five on five, sits at 11-6-5 with 27 points, about four more than our expected points.

The best unit is a newer one: Filip Forsberg, Nils Hoglander and Shane Wright have outscored opponents 9-2 with 56% of the expected goals. The Steven Stamkos, Ryan O'Reilly and Mavrik Bourque line has been the problem, outscored 10-4 at 42%, even as Stamkos keeps scoring on the power play. Josi and Adam Wilsby drive play; Brady Skjei and Nick Perbix get outchanced. Our odds put Andrew Brunette's team at 60% to make the playoffs. Whether that holds depends on Saros staying this good.
